name: Return on Investment (International)
description: Evaluate whether an investment paid off, including a return realized in a foreign market.
formula: Net Gain = Revenue Gain + Cost Savings; ROI % = Net Gain / Investment Cost. At advanced difficulty, Cost Savings is instead realized in a foreign currency: Net Gain = Revenue Gain + (Foreign Cost Savings × FX Rate).
business_contexts: a manufacturer weighing whether a new packaging line was worth the money it cost
a retailer assessing whether a store remodel was worth its cost
a logistics company assessing whether a new routing system was worth its cost
a consumer goods company evaluating a completed plant upgrade with savings realized at its European facility
a hospital system assessing whether new equipment was worth its purchase price
question_patterns: Relative to what it cost, how much did the client actually get back from this investment?
Expressed as a percentage of what was spent, how well did this investment pay off?
What is the ROI once the foreign-currency portion of the return is converted to dollars?
As a percentage of the original outlay, what did the client gain from this investment?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate net gain = revenue_gain + cost_savings
Step 2: Calculate ROI = net gain / investment_cost × 100
Step 1 (advanced): Convert foreign savings = foreign_cost_savings × fx_rate
Step 2 (advanced): Calculate net gain = revenue_gain + converted foreign savings
Step 3 (advanced): Calculate ROI = net gain / investment_cost × 100
key_insight: ROI measures net gain relative to what was put in — and when part of that gain arrives in a foreign currency, it has to be converted before it can be added to the rest.
common_mistakes: Adding the foreign-currency figure directly without converting it first
Dividing by the gain instead of the cost of investment
Forgetting to subtract the cost of investment before dividing, which reports gross return instead of net
framework_soundbite: ROI is net gain over cost — and every dollar of that gain has to actually be in dollars before you add it up.
